answer: Jetty-tide pulse proof: a $22 tide sensor bolted to one real jetty piling is the price of a voyage. Each epoch the sensor reports the tide's pulse at that piling, and the verifier matches the reading against the NOAA tide log for the same harbour — a forged tide misses by centimetres and fails on the spot. A copied reading repeats the same pulse, so the pair is caught in one match. Sensors are cheap and jetties are not: a harbour holds only so many pilings, and a sensor on dry land reports no tide at all.
